gloss: broken speech, few words of a language

definitions.gloss: broken speech, smattering of a language
definitions.explanation: Limited, halting speech in a foreign language. Describes the ability to speak only a few basic words or phrases, typically with poor grammar and pronunciation.

examples.japanese: {片言|かたこと}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{話|はな}した→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{片言|かたこと}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{聞|き}いて→聞く：00483_kiku⟧きた。
examples.english: She asked for directions in broken English.

examples.japanese: {片言|かたこと}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{一生懸命|いっしょうけんめい}→一生懸命：01280_isshoukenmei⟧⟦{伝|つた}えよう→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{姿勢|しせい}→姿勢：00371_shisei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ。
examples.english: What matters is the effort to communicate, even in broken speech.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ to modify a language: {片言|かたこと}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧ (broken Japanese), {片言|かたこと}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧ (broken English). Not derogatory — it simply describes a low level of fluency and is often used self-deprecatingly or with sympathy.

NOTE ON READING:
Also sometimes read as かたげん in more formal or literary contexts, but かたこと is the standard modern reading.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {片言|かたこと}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧: broken Japanese
- {片言|かたこと}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧: to speak haltingly
- {片言|かたこと}⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧: though only in broken speech
